issues.title: Inconsistent observation-count index
issues.failure_explanation: The surrounding setup declares observations through ell with ell at least two, but the cost sums from ell=1 to n without defining n. Thus the displayed general objective has no specified upper bound as written.
issues.overall_effect: The introductory general cost function is not formally well-defined. The later two-observation objective supplies its own upper bound, so no old formal result depends on this notation defect.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a distinct dummy index and the observation count already declared in the setup: write the objective as f(q) = sum from j=1 to ell of |q^{-1} a_j q - b_j|^2. No later result requires alteration.
issues.why_classification: The old source lists exactly ell observations and states ell >= 2, so summation over those listed observations is uniquely forced; n is merely an isolated unbound count symbol. Correcting the indices is transcriptional and requires no mathematical inference or downstream repair.

issues.title: Unsquared norm in the pairwise-similarity proof
issues.failure_explanation: Equation eq:NORM_OF_QUAT_SUM expands a squared norm, but the proof equates that degree-two expression to an unsquared norm. For the admissible choice a1=a2=b1=b2=i, the outer expression is 4 while the middle norm is 2. Squaring both middle norms restores the calculation used to compare the real products.
issues.overall_effect: The characterization proof does not literally establish its required real-product equality, and that equality is subsequently used in the perpendicular-components lemma and the main solution theorem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In eq:NORM_OF_QUAT_SUM_A1A2_B1B2, square both middle norms, replacing |a_1+a_2| and |b_1+b_2| by |a_1+a_2|^2 and |b_1+b_2|^2. The existing comparison and all listed downstream uses then proceed unchanged.
issues.why_classification: Both outer expressions are explicitly the expansions of squared norms supplied by eq:NORM_OF_QUAT_SUM, so the omitted exponents are uniquely forced by the old source. Restoring them corrects the transcription without changing any inference, proof construction, statement, or downstream guarantee.

issues.title: Zero parameter admitted in quaternion square root

failure_location.quote: where $\qp$ is either an arbitrary pure quaternion if $\qa$ is a negative real

diagnostic_evidence.quote: A quaternion $\qa$ is called unit if $\Abs{\qa} = 1$ and it is called pure if $\rea = 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: For a nonzero negative real radicand, the old statement permits any pure p. Taking p=0 is admissible under the stated definition of pure quaternion, but p/|p| then becomes 0/0 and the advertised square-root construction is undefined.
issues.overall_effect: One expressly permitted parameter choice fails to produce a quaternion. Valid nonzero choices, and results requiring only a valid square root, are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict p to an arbitrary nonzero pure quaternion in the negative-real branch. Then p/|p| is defined and still ranges over every unit pure direction, preserving the complete square-root family.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine missing admissibility condition on a quotient, not merely a harmless symbol substitution. Nevertheless, excluding only p=0 is a standard, short, local nondegeneracy repair that preserves the construction and all valid square roots with no substantive loss or propagation.

issues.title: Unbound parameter in the main solution theorem
issues.failure_explanation: The old parameter list binds lambda_1, lambda_2, and mu, while both the nonzero condition and eq:SOLUTION_HOMOGENEOUS_WAHBAS_EQUATION_Q1 use mu_1. Consequently, the stated solution family contains an unquantified parameter and an unused quantified one.
issues.overall_effect: The main theorem's advertised parameterization and admissibility condition are not formally defined as written, although the intended parameter name is unambiguous from the formula.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the listed first-stage parameter mu by mu_1 and make the corresponding first-stage proof occurrence use mu_1 consistently. Retain the existing admissibility condition and q_1 formula unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The admissibility condition and q_1 formula consistently use mu_1, while the proof later distinguishes a separate mu_2, so the intended binding is uniquely determined by the old source. This is a transcriptional parameter-name mismatch requiring no mathematical or downstream repair.
